# ZipCloseFailureUnchecked

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Writing an archive is not complete until finalization succeeds. Check the close result before returning success. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
function archive($p){$z=new ZipArchive();if($z->open($p,ZipArchive::CREATE)!==true){return false;}$z->addFromString("a.txt","a");$z->close();return true;}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Check archive finalization before returning success.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- A proven ZipArchive receiver has a successful checked open, then addFromString/addFile mutation, and a discarded close result followed by unconditional literal true return from the containing function. Highlight close; no success-name heuristics.
- The initial supported proof is consecutive checked-open rejection guard, archive mutation, discarded close, and return true statements.
- Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods; user-defined lookalikes are excluded. Follow only bounded local proof in one lexical scope.
- Emit one finding per violating operation, not per supporting evidence statement. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Do not report unresolved or shadowed builtin names, unknown values, or incomplete receiver/type provenance. Unknown calls, aliases escaping, and intervening writes invalidate local proof. Similar code outside the stated detection contract is not a finding.
- Both standard suppression forms suppress this native ID.

## Fix

None. Choosing a repair requires intent or additional runtime information.

## PHP versions

Available throughout supported PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced builtin/extension is available. Respect syntax/version-specific receiver contracts; unavailable APIs are not this rule’s concern.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ZipCloseFailureUnchecked": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ZipCloseFailureUnchecked
```
